newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: JSE electronic trading ups liquidity by half.
newsitem.headline: JSE electronic trading ups liquidity by half.

text.p: The Johannesburg Stock Exchange said on Tuesday that liquidity had increased to nearly 13 percent this year, under the JET electronic trading system, compared to under nine percent in the previous year.
"Liquidity for the year ended May 31, 1997 was 12.87 percent compared to 8.58 percent for the year ended May 31, 1996, representing a 50 percent increase," it said in a statement.
"Trading for the year ended May 31, 1997 compared to the (previous) year shows substantial increases in value and volume of shares traded, as well as number of deals."

The JSE introduced electronic trading on a phased basis from March 8, 1996. The entire market was converted by June 7, 1996 and with effect from June 10, 1996, exactly one year ago, all shares were trading electronically, it said.
"During the year, JET has experienced some minor setbacks but overall availability has been 99 percent which is quite phenomenal for the implementation of a new computer system."
It said liquidity peaked at 17.3 percent for April 1997.

Deals during the JET year rose by 89 percent (1.82 million versus 0.96 million), volumes of shares traded increased by 86 percenty (12.44 billion versus 6.67 billion), and value traded increased by 66 percent (144.67 billion rand versus 87.22 billion rand).
